brief: A GS desk morning note opens with a risk-on bounce (tech-led S&P futures up, Asia mixed, Europe soft on France, VIX down) after last week's selloff, against ongoing Ukraine/Russia and France geopolitical escalation. Industrials/transports names that already reported (AYI, FUL, RPM, FAST, DAL, JBHT) show soft September topline and broad cost inflation (oil, freight, medical), but muted stock reaction, which the desk attributes to very low gross exposure. China data beat on trade (exports/imports up 36.3%/31.0% yoy, record $133.5bn surplus) but PPI beat consensus while CPI missed, a divergence GS reads as weak domestic demand, prompting it to raise its PPI forecast and cut its CPI forecast. Prime brokerage shows US equities net sold for the week, driven by Single Stock long/short unwinds, with 8 of 11 sectors sold and rotation into defensives (Health Care, Comm Svcs, Staples) out of cyclicals. The note then previews Q3 earnings for GE, GM, MMM, NOC, RTX, CSX, PKG, TSLA, URI and WCN with implied moves, valuation, and positioning/short-interest context.
